newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares inch toward 1,000-point mark.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares inch toward 1,000-point mark.

text.p: Norwegian shares registered a record close on Tuesday after shaking off continuing worries on foreign markets about interest rate hikes.

But the Oslo Bourse Total index inched just 0.02 percent higher to finish at 992.65 points. Following a weak start influenced by foreign markets, the index surged to an intra-day life high of 996.34 points before losing ground again.
"There was a tendency to profit-taking in some shares such as Elkem and Norsk Hydro today, but Elkem also fell because aluminium stocks were higher than expected," one dealer said.
Turnover was heavy at roughly one billion crowns.
Metal maker Elkem's A share fell 1.3 percent to 112 crowns while industrial giant Norsk Hydro shed 0.4 percent to close at 351.50 crowns.
Saga Petroleum continued to rise on high oil prices, its A share now closing 2.2 percent higher at 116.50 crowns.
Dealers remained optimistic the Total index would soon break through the psychological 1,000-point mark.
"All we need is one or two good days in the United States," one said.
